subtitle: "Micromechanics and poromechanics of jointed rock media, and the computational tools to use them."
toc: true

Rock masses are rarely continuous. They are cut by families of joints — fractures that
are both weaker and far more permeable than the intact rock between them — so that
deformation and fluid flow happen in two coupled systems: the pores of the rock matrix
and the network of joints. My research builds continuum models of this double-porosity
behavior from the mechanics of the constituents, and puts them to work in finite element
computations at the scale of engineering structures.

## Micromechanics of jointed rock

The starting point is a homogenization approach. Long joints are treated as interfaces
whose normal and tangential stiffnesses, spacing and orientation enter the effective
properties of the rock mass; short joints are handled with Eshelby-based schemes of the
Mori–Tanaka type. The result is a set of poroelastic coefficients — drained stiffness,
two Biot tensors, two Biot moduli and a coupling modulus — for a double-porosity medium
in which matrix and joints exchange fluid.

The formulation is the subject of my doctoral thesis, supervised by Prof. Samir Maghous
at [PPGEC / UFRGS](https://www.ufrgs.br/ppgec/), and of a paper currently under review
(see [Publications](publications.qmd)).

## Coupled poromechanics

The same micromechanical structure lends itself to richer constitutive behavior. Ongoing
work extends the double-porosity formulation to

- **time-dependent joints** (poroviscoelasticity, hereditary coefficients and aging),
- **thermal and chemical couplings** (thermoporoelasticity and chemoporoelasticity,
  including osmotic effects),
- **partially saturated media**, with two fluids in each porous system,
- **elastoplastic constituents**, with the two effective stresses that the two porous
  systems call for.

## Finite element computation

Models are only useful once they can be computed. I develop and maintain
[GEOMECH3D](software.qmd#geomech3d), a three-dimensional finite element program for Biot
poroelasticity, and [GEOMECH3D-DP](software.qmd#geomech3d-dp), its double-porosity
counterpart, which solves the symmetric indefinite system of the coupled
displacement–pressure–pressure problem. Both are driven from GiD® through dedicated
problem types.

## Field-scale applications

The models are confronted with documented case studies of deep tunnels in fractured rock
masses, where the drainage of the rock mass by the excavation induces surface settlements
and long-term changes in pore pressure. These comparisons test whether the coefficients
obtained from field data for the joints and the matrix reproduce the observed behavior
with both mechanisms acting in a single continuum.
